title: The friendship paradox
text: Social scientists have noticed a curious pattern: on average, your friends have more friends than you {{1}}. This 'friendship paradox' is not an insult {{2}} at your social life but simple mathematics. Popular people appear in more people's lists of friends, so when you sample friends randomly, you {{3}} up oversampling popular people. The same logic {{4}} why your sexual partners' partners seem busier, why co-authors have more publications than you, and why the people you follow online seem to lead richer lives. Researchers {{5}} that the effect can distort our judgement: we compare ourselves with an unusually glittering sample of humanity and find ourselves {{6}}. The paradox even has practical {{7}}: during a flu outbreak, checking the friends of randomly chosen people detects epidemics weeks earlier, because well-connected individuals {{8}} infections first.
